mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, increasing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE < 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth, as measured by GDPC1, indicates strong economic demand, which positively impacts corporate revenues and thus S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive over a 5-year period, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 growth is strong and UNRATE is low, it indicates a robust economy, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the joint effect of GDPC1 and UNRATE does not significantly predict SPX returns in out-of-sample testing, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 indicates strong supply chain activity, which is positive for S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO > 105, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in one month signals a sharp tightening of monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) above 330 indicate inflationary pressures that may lead to monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when CPIAUCSL > 330 during late-cycle expansions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive over a 5-year period, the hypothesis is rejected.
